concepts.def: Component sensing the environment or user (switch, sensor, microphone) and feeding a signal into an electronic system.
Component performing the system's logic, ranging from simple op-amps to microcontrollers like the Arduino Uno (released 2010).
Component producing the system's response, such as LED, motor, speaker or display.
Integrated circuit containing CPU, memory and I/O on a single chip, programmable for embedded control applications.
Component limiting current flow, with values typically marked by colour bands following the standard E12 or E24 series.
Digital building block performing Boolean operations such as AND, OR and NOT, fundamental to all digital electronics.

Electronic Systems — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Electronic Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Electronic Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
